status_summary: Leadership aligned with the Administration replaced the prior leadership early: the International Broadcasting Advisory Board members were reported terminated in late January 2025, and Victor Morales was named acting CEO in a staff email of 2025-03-03, an appointment in which the district court later saw no apparent defect. On 2026-03-07 Judge Royce Lamberth (D.D.C., Widakuswara v. Lake, No. 1:25-cv-1015, ECF 219) held that Kari Lake, styled acting CEO from 2025-07-31 to 2025-11-19, could not serve under the Vacancies Act and that Morales's delegations to her were unlawful, so her actions in that role have no force or effect, and on 2026-05-14 (ECF 241) the court denied the government's motion to reconsider the ruling that those actions cannot be ratified. On 2026-03-12 the White House sent the nomination of Sarah B. Rogers as CEO to the Senate, TheWrap reported that Deputy Secretary of State for Management and Resources Michael Rigas was named acting CEO, and a senator's letter of 2026-03-18 is addressed to Rigas as acting CEO; the Senate Foreign Relations Committee held Rogers's hearing on 2026-07-30 and no confirmation was found. The stage is implemented because acting leadership chosen by the Administration displaced the holdover leadership and an acting CEO is reported serving while a nominee awaits confirmation, though a court held one acting tenure unlawful.

timeline.event: A report said the Office of Personnel Management had notified all members of the International Broadcasting Advisory Board in late January 2025 that they were terminated.

Axios reported that Victor Morales was named acting USAGM CEO in a staff email of 2025-03-03, with Kari Lake serving as a special adviser who could not formally lead VOA until a nominee for a related post was confirmed.

NPR reported that Lake, who had run the agency as a senior adviser and then deputy CEO, assumed the acting CEO role in late July 2025 after Morales was placed on leave, and that legal experts questioned whether she qualified under the Vacancies Act.

Judge Lamberth (D.D.C., Widakuswara v. Lake, No. 1:25-cv-1015, ECF 219) grants the plaintiffs partial summary judgment, holding that Lake could not serve as acting CEO under 5 U.S.C. 3345 and that Morales's delegations to her violated 5 U.S.C. 3347(b), so her actions as acting CEO from 2025-07-31 to 2025-11-19 have no force or effect and cannot be ratified; the court sees no apparent defect in Morales's own appointment.
timeline.source: U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia, ECF 219

timeline.event: The White House sent the nomination of Sarah B. Rogers to be USAGM Chief Executive Officer to the Senate.

TheWrap reported that Michael Rigas, Deputy Secretary of State for Management and Resources, was named acting CEO, after government lawyers told the court that no one was serving as acting CEO following the ruling.

The district court (ECF 241) denies the government's motion for reconsideration of the 2026-03-07 holding that actions Lake took under authority delegated by Morales cannot be ratified under the Vacancies Act.

uncertainties: The 2026-03-07 memorandum opinion (ECF 219) and the 2026-05-14 order denying reconsideration (ECF 241) were read on storage.courtlistener.com on 2026-10-18; the opinion's remedy section was cut off in the text extraction (again on 2026-10-26, ending on page 16), so the exact scope of the actions given no force or effect under 5 U.S.C. 3348(d) is not fully confirmed, and the opinion says the defendants had not identified a current acting CEO. The government appealed the 2026-03-07 and 2026-03-17 orders on 2026-03-19 (D.C. Cir. Nos. 26-5086 and 26-5087, per the Clearinghouse docket), the district court denied a partial stay pending appeal on 2026-03-20, and the D.C. Circuit on 2026-03-31 stayed only the return-to-work requirement of the 2026-03-17 orders and denied motions to dismiss the appeals as moot, without addressing the Vacancies Act holding; no appellate ruling on that holding was found as of 2026-10-26. Rigas's acting role rests on TheWrap and Columbia Journalism Review reporting and on a senator's letter of 2026-03-18 addressed to him as acting CEO (blumenthal.senate.gov), and was not confirmed on an agency, State Department or court site; the Clearinghouse docket summary names no acting CEO, and whether his service meets the Vacancies Act was not examined. The 2026-03-07 opinion states that the court saw no apparent defect in Morales's appointment as acting CEO. The board removal is described only as late January 2025 by a secondary report. The nomination is confirmed through the White House notice; the Senate Foreign Relations Committee hearing page of 2026-07-30 lists the nominee for both CEO and Under Secretary for Public Diplomacy and notes no vote, and no committee vote or confirmation was found as of 2026-10-13. The stage is a judgment: acting leadership chosen by the administration existed for most of the period, but part of it was held unlawful and there was a reported gap with no acting CEO in March 2026.
